overview: Bodmin Jail is a gloomy old county prison on the edge of Bodmin, built in 1779 and closed in 1927, and it’s a gripping way to spend a rainy morning. It was the first prison in Britain to give prisoners their own cells, and more than 50 public hangings took place here over the years; the last execution was in 1909.
Part of the old jail is now a museum about crime and punishment in Georgian and Victorian Cornwall, and part has become a hotel. It’s mostly indoors, so it’s a sound plan B when the weather turns.

expect.title: Cells and corridors
expect.text: You walk through original cell blocks and corridors, with the stories of people held here and the grim punishments of the time, right down to the execution pit.

expect.title: The Dark Walk
expect.text: An immersive walk-through that tells the jail’s history with sound and lighting effects. It’s meant to be atmospheric and a bit scary, so it may be too much for younger children.

expect.title: Tours and ghost nights
expect.text: Go self-guided or join a guided tour. The jail plays up its haunted reputation too, with evening paranormal experiences for brave adults.

expect.title: A wartime secret
expect.text: Near the end of the First World War, national records including the Domesday Book were kept here for safety.

goodToKnow.label: Getting there
goodToKnow.text: It’s a couple of minutes from Bodmin town centre, signed with brown tourist signs. If you park on nearby streets, be considerate of the neighbours.

goodToKnow.label: Access
goodToKnow.text: If you have mobility needs, phone ahead to talk through what’s possible.

goodToKnow.label: Food
goodToKnow.text: The Moor Café on site is open every day.

week.text: Bodmin sits in the middle of Cornwall, so the jail is easy to reach from either coast. Save it for a wet day, or combine it with a walk in the woods at Cardinham or a visit to Lanhydrock nearby.

pairWith.why: a grand house and gardens just south of town
a small free-to-browse museum in town

tips: Check the age guidance for the Dark Walk if you have young or easily spooked children.
It’s a handy stop on the way to or from the A30 on travel day.
